testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Why do dry bulk tanks require special care?

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and their loads often shift during driving. Be extra careful when turning and taking curves.

questions.question: Most CDL holders have ____ licenses.
questions.correctAnswerText: Non-excepted
questions.explanation: Most CDL holders who drive commercial vehicles across state lines have non-excepted licenses.

questions.question: When driving on the expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive above the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: On the expressway during your driving test, maintain proper lane position and spacing. Always check your mirrors to see traffic in all directions.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, you should check that:

options.text: The lift is the proper color.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lift is not leaking.
questions.explanation: Check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, and missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and securely locked.

questions.question: When inspecting brakes, the brake pads should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil or grease.
questions.explanation: Brake shoes and pads must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: When checking tires, which of the following is NOT a problem?

options.text: Radial and bias-ply tires used together
Tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch on the front tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch on the front tires
questions.explanation: Problems to check for include: too much or too little air pressure, mixing radial and bias-ply tires, tread less than 4/32 inch on front tires, and tread less than 2/32 inch on other tires.

questions.question: Friction inside a brake drum happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: If an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) malfunctions, what happens?

options.text: A yellow lamp will light up on the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow lamp will light up on the control panel.
questions.explanation: A yellow warning light on the instrument panel will turn on if the ABS is not working correctly.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use the low beam lights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Do this even during the day.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, cargo weight should be:

options.text: Placed only on the left side, if possible.
Placed only on the right side, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in the trailer. If weight is too high, the vehicle can tip over.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, once air pressure is lost and the spring brakes come on, what can you do?

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks will automatically refill to a safe level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. You can use this tank to temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Push the correct control to release the brakes for a short time. This lets you move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to finish the trip quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy while driving, safely pull off the road and sleep. Drinks like coffee can be dangerous. When they wear off, you may feel extreme tiredness.

questions.question: You are transporting 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer. What is the minimum number of tie-downs you need?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three tie-downs
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, no matter the size, needs at least two tie-downs.

questions.question: How should you do a standard parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your right. Back into the space while bringing the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, are drivers allowed to exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: No, they are not permitted to stop and exit.
Yes, only if the vehicle is in reverse.
Yes, only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.
questions.explanation: Before exiting to check your vehicle's position, put it in neutral and set the parking brake. You may check the position a maximum of two times. For straight line backing, you may look only once.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Increase distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Avoid using tricks to help others pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, increase your following distance, avoid quick moves, and don't use tricks like flashing lights. Speeding up makes the danger worse. The tailgater will just follow at a higher speed.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, your vehicle is found to be over-length. What should you do?

options.text: Trim the length of the load.
Check that flags and lights for the oversize load are secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that flags and lights for the oversize load are secure.
questions.explanation: If your load is oversize, make sure all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly fastened. Check that you have all required permits.

questions.question: When looking in your mirrors, why should you frequently check your tires?

options.text: To see if tires are rolling properly.
To check if the tread is sufficient.
To judge tire size compared to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for tire fires.
questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to spot tire fires early. Tire fires can happen when a tire is under-inflated, when dual tires touch, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: What can happen if your vehicle has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It may get better fuel mileage.
It may be harder to see the road.
The tires may not handle the weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may tip over.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity is dangerous. Cargo piled high or heavy cargo on top increases the risk of your vehicle tipping over.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Keep four points of contact with the vehicle.
You can face the road before your exit is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, stay in contact with the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will result in automatic failure.

questions.question: Heavy steering often means:
questions.correctAnswerText: A front tire has failed.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If your steering feels different, exit the road safely and check your tires.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow instructions.
Not change lanes if you don't want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic first.
questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you will change lanes multiple times. Always check traffic and use proper signals before changing lanes. Change lanes smoothly and safely.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix it.
Ask you to fix the problems.
Stop you from driving until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop you from driving until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a vehicle unsafe, they can take it out of service until it is repaired.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo can:

options.text: Injure the driver during a sudden stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Injure the driver during a sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly loaded and secured. During a sudden stop, unsecured cargo can injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards must be at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: 10.75 inches.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10.75 inches square.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Need repair but not right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very dangerous.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports your vehicle and load. Check for broken spring hangers, leaves, shock absorbers, u-bolts, and frame parts. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver uses high beams, you should:

options.text: Flash your high beams to remind them to switch.
Look to the right side of your lane until they pass.
Pull to the side of the road until they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of your lane until they pass.
questions.explanation: When an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, look toward the right side of the road until it passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: When a construction worker is near the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In work zones with workers on or near the road, always reduce your speed.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful because you cannot control what is far away.
Good practice to spot hazards early.
Only needed when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good practice to spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 12 to 15 seconds. This helps you see hazards early and have time to respond.

questions.question: A stopped bus is:

options.text: Not a concern if no one is getting off.
Should not be on the road.
Always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front or behind it, and the bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They let rain water enter the tanks.
They remove water and oil from the tanks.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: What happens to your braking distance if you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph?
questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples.
questions.explanation: Higher speed increases your vehicle's power and braking distance. Doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph makes your braking distance four times longer.

questions.question: What should you look for when checking tire condition during vehicle inspection?

options.text: The insides should be more worn than the outsides.
The outsides should be more worn than the insides.
The middles should be more worn than the outsides.
The tires should have even wear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires should have even wear.
questions.explanation: During vehicle inspection, check that tire tread is worn evenly across all tires.

questions.question: Which of these is most likely to cause hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using tires with worn tread
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens on wet roads when tire pressure is low or tire tread is worn. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: How should you use road speed to decide when to shift gears?

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as your guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle's manual to learn the rpm range for each gear. Also learn which speeds work for each gear, watch your speedometer, and shift up as needed.

questions.question: Which of these crimes would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.correctAnswerText: Littering
questions.explanation: Certain crimes disqualify a person from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include arson, robbery, and crimes of dishonesty, fraud, or misrepresentation. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime disqualification.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when using a turn signal?

options.text: Cancel the turn signal after completing the turn.
Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is done.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change. Then turn off the signal so other drivers are not confused.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what pressure must be built up in both systems?
questions.correctAnswerText: At least 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire fails while driving?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after you stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. Once it slows down, brake gently, pull off the road, and stop. Then check your tires.

questions.question: What should you do if you are unsure whether your vehicle can fit under an upcoming bridge?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit safely under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: Where can you find the tire load rating?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure. You will find this number printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, you may hear a loud bang. The truck will be affected:

options.text: Only if the damaged tire is near the front of the truck.
Only if the truck is hauling a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: There is usually a short delay between when you hear the tire fail and when the truck is affected. Because of this delay, you might think the noise came from another vehicle.

questions.question: To leave a stop as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So that you must back up to leave your parking space.
So that you can pull forward to leave your parking space.
On the side of a roadway, not in a parking lot.
By backing into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that you can pull forward to leave your parking space.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous, so avoid it when you can. Park in a way that lets you pull forward to leave your space.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:

options.text: Steer with one hand to keep the other hand free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In work zones, follow the posted speed limits. Slow down if road or weather conditions are bad. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet of your current position.
Within 1,000 feet of your current position.
Within your view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Always drive in a way that lets your vehicle stop completely within the distance you can see ahead on the road.

questions.question: The ____ tells a driver how much pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: A vehicle with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: If exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Maintain a firm grasp on the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a firm grasp on the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and always have three points of contact. For a bus, hold the handrail firmly. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: Why do you need to drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains some water which must be drained from the tanks
To allow for a change in air pressure
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains some water which must be drained from the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and compressor oil. If these build up in the system, they can damage the brakes. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Veer from your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Reduce your speed after entering the curve.
Refrain from looking for other vehicles while turning.
Reduce your speed before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve during the driving skills test, slow down enough so you do not need to brake or shift while in the curve. Stay in your lane and keep checking for other traffic.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park in a congested area near trees.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in an open area.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop right away. Park in an open area away from trees, plants, and other vehicles that could catch fire. Do not pull into a service station.
